newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South African share tax cut to 0.25 percent.
newsitem.headline: South African share tax cut to 0.25 percent.

text.p: The marketable securities tax (MST) and stamp duty on share transactions would be cut to 0.25 percent from 0.5 percent from April 1, Finance Minister Trevor Manuel said on Wednesday.
He said in his budget speech that this would cost the government 125 million rand.

"However, it is interesting to note than in 1996/97, these levies were reduced from one percent to 0.5 percent and although we budgeted to collect 200 million rand, our revised estimate is 390 million rand," he said.
The reduction was in line with the recommendations of the Katz commission on taxation and was aimed at improving the competitiveness of the investment climate in South Africa.
Manuel said the government was concerned about the extent to which the exemption from stamp duty for arbitrage transactions was being abused.
The exemption was introduced in 1980 to attract extra business to the Johannesburg Stock Exchange but had resulted in very few foreigners paying stamp duty when they bought shares.
A practice notice had been issued saying that this was not acceptable, but the situation had not changed.
As a result, it had been decided to do away with the exemption as from July 1, 1997.
